question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}$ at the point $(1,0,2,5).$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})=2x \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})=-2y \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})=2z\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(1,0,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,0,2) & =2(1)=2 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,0,2) & =-2(0)=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,0,2) & =2(2)=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-5 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,0,2)+(y-0)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,0,2)+(z-2)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(1,0,2) \\ w-5 & =2(x-1)+0y+4(z-2) \\ w-5 & =2x+4z-10 \\ 2x+4z-w-5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
